# #203 Stall length on the roster ## Parent
#201
## What to build
A coach sees each player's **stall length** on the roster (CONTEXT.md "Stalling"): consecutive committing sessions with no personal record on any exercise in the current program. It counts from the later of the latest personal-record session and the first session under the current program version. After every session commit, the existing best-effort post-commit hook recounts it from the player's ledger with a bounded look-back and stores it in the catalog-side per-assignment roster summary beside the missed-day streak. It is a recount, not an increment. Stall length becomes the roster urgency order's last key before username (longest first). Android and web Coach mode roster rows display it.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Roster rows expose `stall_length`, read from catalog tables only. Listing the roster opens no player ledger. - [ ] After N committing sessions without a personal record, the roster shows stall length N (roster API test through the player commit route). - [ ] A personal record resets stall length to 0. An exercise's first recorded session is a baseline, not a personal record. - [ ] Publishing a new program version starts a fresh count. - [ ] Re-syncing the same workout (same client session id) does not change stall length. - [ ] A session backdated within the correction window is counted in its correct place. - [ ] A failure in the stall recount never fails the workout commit. - [ ] Stall length is the last order key before username. Pure ordering tests cover the tie-break. - [ ] Android and web roster rows show stall length, with widget tests following the existing Coach mode roster tests. - [ ] Schema changes are additive, following the existing roster-summary migration pattern.
